purpose: Isoniazid is used to treat or prevent tuberculosis (TB), a serious infection that mainly affects the lungs. It is often taken along with other TB medicines to fully clear the infection. It can also be used on its own to prevent TB in people who have been exposed to it but are not yet sick.
how_it_works: Isoniazid works by blocking the TB bacteria from building a protective outer wall that they need to survive. Without this wall, the bacteria cannot grow and eventually die off. Think of it like taking away the bricks the bacteria need to build their protective shell.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, or upset stomach are fairly common, especially at first. You might also notice tingling, numbness, or a burning feeling in your hands or feet — this is called peripheral neuropathy. Some people feel tired or have mild headaches while taking this medicine.
warnings: Isoniazid can affect your liver, so it is very important to avoid alcohol while taking it. Let your doctor or pharmacist know right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain, as these can be signs of liver problems. Taking vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) along with isoniazid is often recommended to help prevent nerve-related side effects. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor, even if you feel better.
typical_dosing: For adults, the usual dose is 300 mg taken once daily by mouth, or sometimes 5 mg per kilogram of body weight per day. For prevention of TB, it is usually taken for 6 to 9 months. For active TB treatment, it is taken for at least 6 months along with other TB medicines. It is best taken on an empty stomach, but if it upsets your stomach you can take it with a small meal.
